html:
The Waco were a band of the Wichita peoples, who spoke a Caddoan language and lived in villages of grass houses, farming maize, beans and squash and hunting bison. The map shows them in 1492 on the Brazos River in central Texas, where the city of Waco now stands and takes their name; they are recorded there in the late 1700s and early 1800s, after the Wichita bands moved south from Kansas and Oklahoma under pressure from the Osage.

Their village on the Brazos was a trading place for horses and goods with the Comanche and with French and American traders. Pressure from Texan settlers and wars pushed them from the valley in the 1830s and 1840s. In 1859 they were moved to Indian Territory, and today their descendants belong to the Wichita and Affiliated Tribes of Oklahoma.
